name: Swiss International Grid
description: 1950s Swiss International Typographic Style: strict mathematical grid, flat solid color fields, objective neutrality, and engineered white space.
magic_media_keywords: Swiss International Typographic Style poster composition, strict mathematical grid with generous structured white space, flat solid color fields, one objective photographic cutout element, clean flat-vector illustration accents, diffused overcast light neutrality, ample uncluttered negative space engineered for typography.
palette_hint: Swiss reduction — signal red (#E30613) on paper white (#F4F4F2), anchored by near-black (#111111) for legible contrast
best_for: corporate annual reports, editorial magazine layouts, and minimalist fashion branding with Helvetica precision

graphic_composition.person_cutout: High-contrast duotone photographic portrait using two colours from the palette, strictly aligned to the mathematical grid (occupying exactly 2-3 grid columns), shot with diffused overcast light for neutral objectivity. The cutout must be a clean geometric crop — no feathered edges, no drop shadow, no gradient fade. The subject gazes toward the headline, creating a directional reading line.
graphic_composition.cta_button: Flat rectangular button with sharp 0 px border-radius, filled with one solid palette colour and white or black Helvetica text (the colour that yields ≥ 4.5:1 contrast). The button aligns exactly to the grid baseline and spans exactly 2 grid columns. CTA text is 2-3 words, all lowercase per Swiss tradition: 'learn more', 'download now', 'register today'.
graphic_composition.giant_typography: Helvetica Bold or Akzidenz-Grotesk at 6-8× headline scale, set in a light tint (8-12% of the palette's darkest colour) behind the main content block, spanning 4-6 grid columns. The giant type acts as a structural anchor — an architectural element, not decoration. It must touch at least one grid margin exactly.
graphic_composition.badge: Square or near-square geometric badge (no rounded corners) filled with a flat palette accent colour, aligned to grid intersections. Content: a short code ('ISSUE 04', 'A2', '2026') set in Helvetica Regular at exactly 1 grid-unit size. The badge must sit precisely on a grid cross-point with its edges parallel to grid lines.
